title: Guide
intro: A tool for building Genshin Impact combat rotations (who uses what, and when) along a timeline, and checking Skill/Burst cooldowns and buff overlaps. Rotations are saved only in this browser.
articleLink: Intro article for this app (HoYoLAB, in Japanese)

items.1: Open Team Setup and choose the 4 party members (character, constellation, weapon, artifacts).
items.2: Under "Add stint" in the middle of the screen, press a character's button to line up stints (one on-field turn of that character). The same character can appear any number of times.
items.3: Inside each stint, press buttons such as +N +C +tE +hE +Q +D +J +Wait to add actions.
items.4: Check the timeline, Skill/Burst cooldowns, effect durations, buff overlaps and cooldown conflicts on the Gantt chart below.
items.5: For precise numbers, press Apply gcsim (the real simulator measures action times, cooldowns, durations and triggered buffs, and applies them).
items.6: When you are happy with it, use Save as (saved rotation). Copy notation creates a one-line notation you can post on social media.

items.1: Top row: choose a saved rotation, Save, Save as / play and reset (cycle, time, speed 0.5x–2x) / cooldown status (No cooldown conflicts / Cooldown conflicts / Cooldown warnings) / Hide (show or hide the button row below).
items.2: Button row: Guide / Import Chars, Team Setup, Manage Teams, Manage DB / Apply gcsim, Copy gcsim config, Back to app calculation / ER Calc, DPS Calc / Copy notation (and the current notation, with Short/Names switch).
items.3: Build area (list of stints): edit the order and the actions here. The chips of "Quick reorder" above change the stint order at a glance.
items.4: Gantt chart: the horizontal axis is time (seconds). From the top: stint flow, number of overlapping buffs (Synergy), and one row per character (actions, cooldowns, effects, triggered buffs). Zoom with the slider at the top right.

items.1: Where actions are added: when one action is selected with a click, the add buttons insert before it (in the same stint). With nothing selected, or another stint selected, actions are added at the end. Click the stint background to clear the selection.
items.2: Reordering: drag and drop actions (within the same stint; the switch action stays first). Stints can be moved with the card's drag handle, "Up/Down", dragging the quick reorder chips, or dragging on the Gantt chart. After reordering, later times reconnect automatically (serial snapping).
items.3: Action time: change each action's time with ▲▼ (0.05 s, 0.1 s) or by typing a number. For hold skills (hE), you can also set how long to hold. Changed values are marked, and "Back to app calculation" restores them all.
items.4: Delete: the ✕ on an action. For a stint, the delete button on the right of the card (or the × on its quick reorder chip).
items.5: Add memo: you can leave a memo on each stint.

items.1: Ctrl+click actions (Cmd+click on Mac) to select adjacent ones → "Group N". With only one selected, "Repeat 1".
items.2: Set the group's count (▲▼ or a number) and the actions inside are calculated as done that many times in a row. The default is 1.
items.3: The notation becomes 3C (one action 3 times) or 2[N1C] (N1 and C twice).
items.4: Pressing Ungroup lays the actions out as normal actions with the current count (with a count of 3, three repetitions remain).
items.5: Actions inside a group can only be reordered within the group. The whole group can also be moved.

items.1: Cooldown bars (Skill CD, Burst CD): the wait until the action can be used again. Actions with a red mark have a cooldown conflict (used before the cooldown ended).
items.2: Effect bars (shields, fields, transformations, etc.): while the action's effect lasts.
items.3: Dashed-border bars (triggered buffs): effects of passive talents, weapons, artifacts and constellations, colored by type. Carried means the effect continues from the previous cycle.
items.4: Amber border / cooldown warning: triggered buffs placed during their cooldown, special skills outside their window, plunging attacks without their prerequisites, etc. Hover over the bar to see the reason.
items.5: Loop point: the start of the range repeated from the 2nd cycle on. Drag to move it. Playback lets you check the 1st and 2nd cycles.
items.6: Hover over a bar to see its name, timing and description.

items.1: "Apply gcsim" runs the current team and rotation in gcsim (the simulator, running inside your browser) and applies the results at once. Nothing is sent to a server.
items.2: Applied values: action times, Skill/Burst cooldowns, effect durations, and positions and lengths of triggered buffs. If there are cooldown conflicts, it does not run (fix them first).
items.3: To discard applied values and return to the app's calculation (master frames and cooldowns), use "Back to app calculation".
items.4: "Copy gcsim config" gives you the gcsim config (to run it in gcsim elsewhere; conversion warnings are shown too).
items.5: Characters and effects gcsim does not support are marked "Not simulated" and keep the app's calculation.

er.title: Energy Recharge calculation (ER needed for your bursts)

items.1: "ER Calc (gcsim)" in the header finds, with gcsim, the Energy Recharge (total ER%) each character needs so that every burst can go off every lap without waiting for energy, with the current team and rotation. Press "Start calculation"; it takes a few minutes.
items.2: For each character the table shows Typical (the ER at which about 70% of the bursts go off without waiting), Stable (about 90%) and Certain (all bursts go off without waiting; verified in gcsim). Use Certain if you never want a burst to wait. Characters without a burst show "No burst"; if Certain exceeds the search limit (+500%), "Unreachable" is shown.
items.3: "Current" is the total ER with the current team setup (owned-character gear or temporary values). The color shows whether it is enough (green = enough for Certain, yellow = enough for Stable, red = not enough).
items.4: The calculation conditions can be changed on the screen (loop count, cores used, number of seeds, verification precision, enemy particles, wait before a burst). If you change the party or the rotation, the previous result is no longer shown, so calculate again.
items.5: “Check that the Energy Recharge is enough” and its “Check” button: runs the current party and rotation for the chosen number of loops and shows how many times a burst waited for lack of energy (per loop) and the average wait (per wait), per character in a table and as a total. No waits means that Energy Recharge is enough. It works in normal mode (start energy full) and in Abyss mode (start energy 0, with battle conditions), and you do not need to run the ER calculation first.
items.6: The “Energy Recharge” column of the table can be changed per character with 1% up/down buttons (defaults to the current value; “↺” resets it), so you can try whether another value is enough. While it runs, the elapsed and remaining time are shown and “Cancel” stops it. Changing a setting keeps the previous result until you press the button (a note says it is from the previous settings).
items.7: “Loop count” (default 3) and “Number of seeds to try” (default 10) apply to both the calculation and the check. “Re-pick seeds” changes the seed numbers at random so you can see whether another set of seeds gives the same result (it returns to normal when you reopen the screen). The DPS calculation uses the same parts for the loop count (default 5), cores and enemy particles.

abyss.title: Abyss mode (start from 0 energy and check that bursts go off every time)

items.1: The “Normal / Abyss” switch to the right of the title of the Energy Recharge screen changes the mode. The only differences between the two are the start energy (full / 0) and the Abyss battle conditions (none / present). Abyss mode is for rotations like the Abyss ones (actions done only on the first lap + actions that repeat): it checks that burst energy builds up and that the bursts at the repeated positions can go off every time.
items.2: How to build the rotation: in the actions done only on the first lap, use skills only to build burst energy, then put the loop reference point, and fire the bursts after it (the repeated part).
items.3: In Abyss mode the ER calculation starts everyone from 0 energy and also judges the first burst. It runs the loop part of the rotation for a fixed number of loops after the opening (default 3; changeable in the "Loop count" section, which also applies to normal mode; there is no time limit). "The first burst may wait up to … s after its planned time" (default 0.5 s) is how late the first burst may be. If the opening itself fires a burst, no amount of ER lets it go off at the planned time and the result is "Unreachable", so raise this value.
items.4: “Timed particles”: add particles that appear at fixed times (seconds from the start of the battle), for example when a boss shield breaks. They are handled like enemy particles (Energy Recharge applies, and the on-field character gets more) and are calculated as colorless particles. In the Energy Recharge calculation, whatever does not fit gcsim’s single particle setting (two or more timed particles, or timed particles used together with the enemy’s periodic particles) is added to the energy timeline by the app (such a result is “calculation only”, with no final gcsim check). Limitation: the sufficiency check runs on gcsim alone, so with several timed particles only the latest one takes effect, and with a timed particle the enemy’s periodic particles do not take effect (the screen shows a notice).
items.5: "Saved battle conditions": save the battle conditions (loop count, first-burst wait, timed particles, enemy particles, no-damage periods) under a name and call them up per boss (up to 30; included in the backup). Click a name to put it into the fields; saving under the same name overwrites it.
items.6: Abyss-mode results are saved separately from normal mode (switching keeps the other mode’s conditions and results). The DPS calculation can be used in either mode (it does not use the Abyss battle conditions). During a no-damage period (seconds from the start of the battle; several allowed), energy that requires dealing damage (Favonius-type particles, Albedo C1, and so on) is removed from the energy timeline (this is a “calculation only” result with no final gcsim check). In the rotation display, the Sacrificial skill cooldown reset does not happen during such a period (it is not reflected in the gcsim runs of the ER calculation).

owned.title: Owned characters (use your HoYoLAB build and stats)

items.1: Install the browser extension once (desktop Chrome, Edge or Firefox). Open "Import Chars" in the header and follow the steps shown for your browser (Chrome / Edge: get the zip → extract → turn on "Developer mode" in chrome://extensions → "Load unpacked". Firefox: get the .xpi → "Install Add-on From File" in about:addons). Then reload this page.
items.2: In a browser logged in to HoYoLAB, use it with your own account (the "Character Details" privacy setting can stay off for your own UID). Enter that account's Genshin UID in the import screen and press "Import" to bring in the level, talents, weapon and artifacts of all your characters. The data is stored only in this browser (it is not sent to the operator's servers). For another account's UID, HoYoLAB does not provide the details, so only the characters whose details that account has made public in the in-game "Character Showcase" are imported from Enka.Network (an unofficial service); the owner must have set this up in the game.
items.3: You can import again at any time (after changing equipment, import again). "Delete imported data" removes it.
items.4: When you pick a character in the party settings, if it has been imported, its owned build and stats are applied automatically (constellation, weapon, refinement, artifacts, plus level, talents, weapon level and artifact stats). Imported characters get an "Owned" tag in the character lists of the party settings and the DB manager.
items.5: The box above the selected slot shows what is in use. With "Owned character's build & stats applied", gcsim uses those values; with "Defaults applied", it uses the defaults (Lv90, talents 9, the weapon and artifact set recommended by the Genshin Wiki, and artifact stats built from those recommendations; for characters without Wiki data, the artifact stats follow a rough ATK / HP / DEF / EM profile and the weapon and set stay as currently selected). The button on the right switches between "Use owned build & stats" and "Use defaults".
items.6: "Edit stats" changes the values other than constellation, weapon and artifacts (character and weapon level, talents, total artifact stats). Saving switches to "Defaults applied" and the saved values become this slot's defaults. The screen shows the final stats calculated by gcsim (reference), updated 2 seconds after you change a value. Changing the weapon, artifacts, refinement or constellation by hand also stops applying the owned build.
items.7: For the Traveler, switch the story quest "True Moon" with the "True Moon" option in the party settings (it cannot be read from HoYoLAB). Characters not implemented in gcsim can be added to a party, but gcsim calculations cannot run. The required energy recharge calculation also uses the party-setting values (owned values or saved defaults); only the artifact Energy Recharge is replaced by the value being swept. The "Current" column of the result table shows the Energy Recharge of the current settings, colored by whether it reaches the required value.
items.8: The setup steps and usage are also explained in an article (<articleLink>HoYoLAB, in Japanese</articleLink>).

items.1: Your edits are saved automatically in this browser (nothing is sent to a server). They are lost if you clear the browser data.
items.2: Manage Teams: save, load and delete named rotations (slots). A single rotation can also be exported to or imported from a JSON file.
items.3: Back up all data (Manage Teams → JSON backup & share): bundles all saved rotations, the current rotation, settings and the data you created into one file. Use it when moving to another browser or device, or before clearing data.
items.4: Manage DB: sync, edit and add character, weapon and artifact data.

notation.title: Notation (sharing as text)

items.1: "Copy notation" copies the rotation as a one-line string. Example: {{example}}
items.2: You can switch between Short (E, Q, N1, C, etc., written compactly) and Names.
items.3: The part enclosed in {{braces}} is the range repeated from the 2nd cycle on (after the loop point).
items.4: Consecutive Normal Attacks are written N3 (3 times), groups 3C or 2[N1C], and holds hE@2.0s.

notation.example: {Furina E > Citlali E > Furina Q > Xiangling EQ}
